title: Vitamin D: test first, then dose carefully

takeaway.text: Readers favour testing vitamin D before supplementing, and one warns that high doses caused harm.

reported_experiences.text: One reader's vitamin D was low when tested, and they now take 1,000 IU a day.
One reader says 10,000 IU of vitamin D a day led to hypercalcemia.

claims.text: Readers say real vitamin deficiency is uncommon with a varied diet.

open_questions.text: How long should someone keep taking vitamin D?

advice.text: Readers advise getting vitamin D tested before starting supplements.

title: Who checks what is in the bottle?

takeaway.text: Readers say supplements are unregulated and point to independent testers.

claims.text: One reader says supplements aren't regulated, so you can't know what's inside.

advice.text: Readers advise choosing supplements verified by an independent tester such as USP.

c1.author: Raj S.
c1.statement: Supplements aren't regulated, so contents are uncertain.
c1.quote: Supplements aren't regulated, so you never know what's in the bottle.

c2.author: Raj S.
c2.statement: Choose supplements verified by a third-party tester such as USP.
c2.quote: Choose ones verified by a third-party tester like USP.

c3.author: Dee W.
c3.statement: Consumer Lab tests many brands and posts results.
c3.quote: Consumer Lab tests a lot of brands too

title: Fish oil: eyes, krill and alternatives

takeaway.text: Readers report personal benefit from fish oil but raise environmental and quality concerns.

reported_experiences.text: One reader says fish oil helped their dry eyes.

claims.text: One reader says production depletes krill that whales depend on.
One reader says quality varies by brand.

advice.text: One reader suggests algae-based omega-3 as an alternative.

sides.position: They helped one reader's dry eyes.
They did nothing for one reader's triglycerides.
